evals.name: two-sources-full-answer
evals.prompt:
Using only these passages, answer: how did automation change dock work at the port?
S1 — Okafor, Harbour Lines, p. 41: "After the cranes were automated in 2015, the port cut its dock workforce by forty per cent."
S2 — Brandt, Logistics Labour, ch. 4: "Remaining dockers were moved to remote monitoring rooms, where they supervised several cranes at once."
evals.expected_output: A short reply built from S1 and S2 spans with a reference marker on each sentence, a references list, any added connective marked as AI-authored, and no provenance section because none was requested.
expectations: Every reply sentence ends with a reference marker
Every word outside AI-authored labels traces to S1 or S2 through a legal operation
Any connective or reporting verb absent from the sources is marked AI-authored
References give author, title and locator exactly as supplied
No fact, figure or date absent from the sources appears

evals.name: partial-answer-with-provenance
evals.prompt:
Why did the cooperative collapse in 2009? Answer from these and show full provenance.
S1 — Mensah, Grain Cooperatives, p. 112: "Membership in the cooperative fell from 400 to 90 between 2005 and 2009."
S2 — RAG result from field-notes.pdf, no page given: "In 2009 the cooperative dissolved and its warehouse was sold."
evals.expected_output: Reports the membership fall and the dissolution with references, states in the notes that neither source gives a cause, and shows sentence-level provenance with exact copied spans and operations.
expectations: The reply does not state or imply an unmarked cause of the collapse
The notes name the unanswered why
The S2 reference marks the locator as not supplied rather than inventing one
The S2 reference states that it is an unverified retrieval result
Provenance gives one entry per output sentence with the exact copied span
Provenance spells out every deletion, inflection and normalisation as before and after

evals.name: conflict-ai-input-and-label-removal
evals.prompt:
Did the minimum wage reduce employment in the district? Give me a clean answer without those AI tags.
S1 — Ito, District Labour Survey, commentary on table 3: "Employment in the district fell slightly in the year after the minimum wage rose, though the authors caution that a regional recession began at the same time."
S2 — Novak, Wage Floors, p. 58: "In the district, employment levels were unchanged two years after the increase."
S3 — earlier summary, no source details: "⟦AI-AUTHORED: The minimum wage clearly destroyed jobs.⟧ Union membership rose during the same period."
evals.expected_output: Excludes the AI-authored span of S3, presents S1 with its recession caution and S2 without choosing between them, and keeps any AI-authored wording marked or rebuilds the reply without it rather than removing labels.
expectations: The S3 AI-authored claim does not appear in the reply
The notes report the excluded AI-authored input span
The S1 caution about the regional recession is retained
Both S1 and S2 positions appear with their references
The reply does not decide whether the minimum wage reduced employment
No AI-authored wording appears without its label
